title: Tokenised motion that respects reduced-motion preferences
iWant: animation that is subtle, consistent, and optional
soThat: the interface feels alive without making anyone ill

acceptanceCriteria.description: All transitions and animations use durations and easings from the motion tokens; unmanaged literal durations do not appear in component styles.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every duration and easing resolves to a motion token

acceptanceCriteria.description: Enter, exit, and state-change transitions sit within the 150-250ms token range with ease-out defaults per ADR-207.
With prefers-reduced-motion set, non-essential animation is disabled; content appears and disappears without translation or scaling effects.
acceptanceCriteria.then: no non-essential motion plays and nothing breaks functionally

acceptanceCriteria.description: No motion autoplays in critical flows: auth surfaces, forms mid-entry, and destructive confirmations are motion-quiet.
Skeleton shimmer and progress animations also honour reduced motion, degrading to static placeholders.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a reduced-motion preference with loading content
acceptanceCriteria.then: placeholders are static and still convey loading via their busy state
